# tokenburn

> tokenburn tracks AI coding usage across tools (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Grok CLI, Hermes Agent, OpenRouter). A small CLI reads each tool's local usage logs and syncs only daily token totals; prompts and code never leave the machine. Users get a private dashboard and an optional public profile at /@username.

## Get started

- Install: `npm install -g use-tokenburn` (macOS, Linux, Windows; Node.js 22.18+)
- Set up: `tokenburn setup` signs in with GitHub, shows what was found and exactly what will upload, asks before the first upload, then turns on automatic sync (the OS runs a quick sync every 30 minutes; nothing stays running in between)
- See numbers in the terminal: `tokenburn stats`
- Publish a profile: `tokenburn profile public`; choose fields with `tokenburn profile show models,tokens,trend`

## What is uploaded

- Uploaded: tokens per model per day, request counts, hashed session ids, Cursor and OpenRouter usage rows
- Never uploaded: prompts and responses, source code, file paths, project and machine names, API keys

## FAQ

- Are prompts or code uploaded? No. Only daily totals per model, request counts and hashed session ids.
- Is my profile public? Not until you publish it from Settings or with `tokenburn profile public`, and you pick each field it shows.
- How is cost estimated? The provider's billed amount where reported (OpenRouter), otherwise the tool's own estimate, otherwise public API list prices. It is not what a subscription costs, and it is always labeled as an estimate.
- Can I delete everything? Yes. Deleting the account in Settings removes the profile and all uploaded usage; `tokenburn forget` clears local data on each machine.

## Public data

- Profile page: https://tokenburn.site/@{username}
- Profile JSON: GET https://tokenburn.site/api/public/{username} (only the fields the owner chose to show)
- Sitemap of public profiles: https://tokenburn.site/sitemap.xml
